unit.title: Subject Pronouns & Ser: Ustedes vs. Vosotros

lesson.title: Pronoun Swap Drills: Trading Names for Él, Ella, and Ellos
lesson.subject: spanish

contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you learned the pronoun chart. Today you put it to work the way real speakers actually use it: swapping a name for a pronombre so you're not repeating it in every sentence.

The rule for choosing él, ella, or ellos is about who you're replacing:

- One boy or man → él
- One girl or woman → ella
- Any group of two or more (all-male or mixed) → ellos

Watch it in action: 'Mateo es de México.' becomes 'Él es de México.' 'Valentina es de Perú.' becomes 'Ella es de Perú.' And 'Mateo y Valentina son de México y Perú.' becomes 'Ellos son de México y Perú.'

One more swap worth knowing: if a sentence includes yo along with other people — 'Ana y yo somos amigos' — the whole group becomes nosotros, because yo is always part of the group being replaced: 'Nosotros somos amigos.'

Swapping names for pronombres is a habit good Spanish speakers do constantly, almost without noticing. Tomorrow the pronoun story gets more interesting: you'll discover how 'you all' and even 'you' change shape depending on which Spanish-speaking country you're in.

items.sentence: Carlos vive en Bogotá. ___ es colombiano.
Diego y Luis estudian español. ___ son buenos amigos.
Mi amigo y yo vamos a la escuela juntos. ___ llegamos temprano.
Valentina toca la guitarra. ___ es muy talentosa.

objectives: State the rule for choosing él, ella, ellos, or nosotros to replace a name or names in a sentence
Correctly swap a name (or names) for the matching pronombre in four practice sentences
materialsNeeded: Device for the cloze activity (optional — can be done orally)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's pronoun chart briefly.
2. Walk through the él/ella/ellos rule with the Mateo/Valentina examples.
3. Point out the special nosotros case (yo + others = nosotros).
4. Complete the pronoun-swap cloze activity together or independently.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview tomorrow's dialect discovery day.
differentiationTips: Struggling: cover él and ella only first (one person each), adding ellos and nosotros once those feel solid
Ready for more: have them swap pronouns in three sentences about their own family or friends
If the child mixes up él/ella, a quick physical cue works well — point to a photo of a boy vs. a girl while saying each word
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. Él (Carlos, one boy). 2. Ellos (Diego y Luis, two boys). 3. Nosotros (mi amigo y yo, includes yo). 4. Ella (Valentina, one girl).
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Delivers Day 2's exact scope-and-sequence design — pronoun-swap drills replacing names with él/ella/ellos — as fast, low-stakes practice building automaticity before Wednesday's more conceptual dialect-comparison work.

generationData.instructions: Replace the underlined name(s) with the correct pronombre: él, ella, ellos, or nosotros.

rows.problem: Sofía es de Chile. → ___ es de Chile.
Pedro y Ana son estudiantes. → ___ son estudiantes.
Mi hermana y yo somos altos. → ___ somos altos.
Explain in your own words: how do you decide between él, ella, and ellos?
